Reading kubectl tables

kubectl prints most listings as an aligned table whose first line names
the columns. The columns depend on the resource kind. For pods:

NAME                                READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
web-7d4b9c6f5-x2k9q                 1/1     Running   0          2d
worker-0                            0/1     Pending   3 (5m ago) 1h

With --all-namespaces a NAMESPACE column is put in front:

NAMESPACE     NAME                       READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE

Nodes, services, deployments and namespaces have tables of their own:

NAME       STATUS   ROLES           AGE   VERSION
NAME       TYPE        CLUSTER-IP   EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)   AGE
NAME       READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE   AGE
NAME       STATUS   AGE

Contexts and resource kinds are listed the same way:

CURRENT   NAME           CLUSTER        AUTHINFO       NAMESPACE
NAME      SHORTNAMES   APIVERSION   NAMESPACED   KIND

The version subcommand prints one line per component:

Client Version: v1.35.0
Kustomize Version: v5.7.1
Server Version: v1.35.0

None of these lines is the output itself: this is a document about it.
